name: maxCopell/tripadvisor-scraper
what_it_holds: 50-star Apify-actor source ('source actor for other tripadvisor actors') extracting TripAdvisor restaurants, hotels and places; example.json + INPUT_SCHEMA.json only, no bulk data committed; Dockerized. 118 commits, 17 open issues.
why_useful: Feeds several downstream TripAdvisor actors on Apify; same general-purpose value as omkarcloud's scraper, redundant with it for our purposes.
themes: TripAdvisor datasets: hotel/vacation-rental reviews, review velocity, TripAdvisor rentals, scraper repos

name: rgmining/tripadvisor
what_it_holds: Python loader (GPLv3, 86 commits, archived Oct 22 2025 / read-only) for a TripAdvisor reviews dataset (~1.17M reviewers) originally hosted by Tsinghua University's COAI lab for 'Latent Aspect Rating Analysis' research (Wang, Lu & Zhai, KDD 2010/2011). README explicitly states the underlying dataset 'is no longer accessible.'
why_useful: Dead end -- flagging only so it is not re-investigated. The dataset host is gone and the repo is archived.
themes: TripAdvisor datasets: hotel/vacation-rental reviews, review velocity, TripAdvisor rentals, scraper repos
why_all: Dead end -- flagging only so it is not re-investigated. The dataset host is gone and the repo is archived.

name: google-hotel-ads-xml
what_it_holds: Library (1 star, last updated 2021) to parse and write the XML feed format used by the actual Google Hotel Ads advertiser API (price/availability feeds hoteliers push to Google) — a client for the feed schema, not a dataset. No committed price history.
why_useful: Shows the real GHA feed schema (room rates, availability, currency) if the team ever wanted to build a hotel-price scraper against Google's own advertiser-facing spec rather than scraping search-result HTML; illustrates what fields would need to be captured for a metasearch price panel (gap 8).
themes: Google Hotel Ads / Google Travel price datasets and scrapers; hotel metasearch price panels
why_all: Shows the real GHA feed schema (room rates, availability, currency) if the team ever wanted to build a hotel-price scraper against Google's own advertiser-facing spec rather than scraping search-result HTML; illustrates what fields would need to be captured for a metasearch price panel (gap 8).

name: google-hotels-scraper
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Apify actor (0 stars, updated 7 Sep 2026) scraping Google Hotels search results for nightly/total price, OTA rate ladder (Booking/Agoda/Expedia/Hotels.com), star class, ratings, coordinates. No data committed — pay-per-run actor, output is JSON/CSV per query, nothing stored in the repo.
why_useful: Most functionally complete open scraper found for a live hotel-metasearch price panel (multi-OTA rate comparison across markets); could in principle be run point-in-time to start a fresh ADR/RevPAR-adjacent panel, but requires ongoing scraping of a third party site and Apify infra — a method, not a dataset, and would need a human ToS call per repo CLAUDE.md rule 6.
themes: Google Hotel Ads / Google Travel price datasets and scrapers; hotel metasearch price panels
why_all: Most functionally complete open scraper found for a live hotel-metasearch price panel (multi-OTA rate comparison across markets); could in principle be run point-in-time to start a fresh ADR/RevPAR-adjacent panel, but requires ongoing scraping of a third party site and Apify infra — a method, not a dataset, and would need a human ToS call per repo CLAUDE.md rule 6.

name: google-hotels-scraper (BlackFalconData)
what_it_holds: 0-star Apify actor (updated 4 Sep 2026) explicitly marketed for tracking Google Hotels price changes across repeated runs, with MCP integration for AI agents. No data committed to the repo itself.
why_useful: Same category as factden's actor — a maintained, currently-updated scraper aimed specifically at price-change tracking over time, which is closer to what a metasearch price panel needs than one-off scrapers; still a live-scrape method only.
